# Exact individual certificates and independent reconstruction

The three new actual candidates are excluded. Both reconstruction methods
agree on every selected representative before the pilot values are compared.
All three have `gcd(L,s_a)=1` and `n mod 25S=0`; their original words fail
a required seven-power divisor. No full witness was found.

| a | k | K | j_5 | gcd(L,s_a) | exact t | first nonzero original n residue |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 1231 | 377 | 468 | 720 | 1 | 4 | 14406 modulo 16807 |
| 1579 | 205 | 467 | 119 | 1 | 1 | 14 modulo 49 |
| 1585 | 450 | 468 | 922 | 1 | 1 | 28 modulo 49 |
| 1591 | 191 | 468 | 780 | 1 | 1 | 42 modulo 49 |
| 1597 | 92 | 468 | 2255 | 1 | 2 | 294 modulo 343 |

All five rows have `n mod 25S=0` at the same actual position and
`F mod 9S=0`. Their exact seven-adic valuations are certified by a zero
residue modulo `7^t` followed by the displayed nonzero residue modulo
`7^(t+1)`, with `t+1<=L-2`. Since nine is a seven-adic unit, the valuations
of n and F agree.

At a=1579, `j_5=119<=K=467` but the actual `k=205`. Its preceding
representative s_b exceeds the preceding length; it is nevertheless used
unchanged. This verifies the in-range-but-wrong-increment failure mode
without assuming anything about the preceding valuation. At a=1231,
`k=377` agrees with each root class through depth four, then `j_5=720>K=468`.
This actual, coprime position is a nonzero depth-four survival control.

## Methods and source boundaries

[`certificates.py`](certificates.py) explicitly imports the inherited
`power-three/individuals.py` Newton seventh-root and modular 3-adic logarithm
engine for method A, at precision 1598. The receipt records its exact path
and SHA-256. The Newton root is also checked against the independent direct
construction `10^(4*7^(-1) mod 3^1598) mod 3^1600`.

Method B uses original decimal blocks, independently implemented in this
file. Binary concatenation forms the all-sevens block modulo S, subtracts
the two changed digits, and solves the resulting power-of-ten condition by
testing all three ternary children at every step. It calls no inherited
arithmetic, no logarithms, and no algebraic root construction. Both methods
recover the selected exponents and their predecessors independently; no
pilot residue selects a ternary child. Low-first ternary digits from method
B are retained in the JSON for full reproduction of the finite blocks.

For each selected current length, the seven-adic lift predicts `c=-4*carry`
modulo seven and tests **all seven children by direct modular exponentiation**
at every lift through depth eight. The receipt retains all child residues,
not only the chosen root. Depth eight is a verification scope for this
lifting rule, not an exclusion threshold for surviving candidates.

Original decimal concatenation independently gives every displayed n residue
and is compared with the sparse F formula. The checker's valuation guard at
64 raises an explicit unresolved-candidate exception if reached. It cannot
classify a depth-capped candidate as excluded. No proposed full witness was
produced. The literal controls separately construct digits, multiply their
product, add their sum, and compare `PS|n` with the complete F predicate on
2,015 pairs with lengths 3 through 64. The literal `(L,s)=(313,51)` control
has `F mod S=0`, `F mod 9S=17496`, and `n mod S=1944`; it fails the original
predicate. The nonzero positive sum control a=25 has `n mod 25S=0` and
seven-residue sequence `0,0,294`. The inherited a=31 base is freshly
rechecked with residue `35 mod49`.

## Complete finite remainder and coverage

All 259 earlier family members `a=31,37,...,1579` are accounted for in exact
order. The two retained independent 256-row receipts are cross-compared;
the a=1567 certificate is reconciled with the pair receipt; the a=1573 and
1579 certificates agree between the two PR #30 methods. These input files
are SHA-256 bound in the new receipt. **Their original independent searches
are inherited, not rerun.** For every one of the 259 rows the new program
freshly checks the position against the precision-1598 kappa, exact length,
range, full `9S` condition, and, when actual, original decimal-block
`n mod25S` and all residues through the first seven-power failure. Thus no
admissible finite case below 1585 is omitted from the corollary's remainder.

The three new exclusions bring the count to **262** named family members,
`a=31+6u`, `0<=u<=261`, through **a=1597**. There are 85 class misses and
177 actual candidates, with valuation histogram `{1:154,2:19,3:3,4:1}`.
The next unchecked family exponent is **1603**. These are isolated family
lengths: consecutive whole-length coverage remains **1 through
1,000,002,000,000 inclusive**. The moving individual family, unrestricted
{5,7} subclass, and wider digit-1 assertion remain open. No Lean
formalization or build was performed for these certificates.

## Reproduction

From the repository root, both commands must succeed and reproduce the
committed receipt exactly:

```sh
pt=research/a398769/five-seven/power-three-carry
PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 "$pt/certificates.py" --check "$pt/certificates.json" > /tmp/power-three-carry-certificates.json
PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -O "$pt/certificates.py" --check "$pt/certificates.json" > /tmp/power-three-carry-certificates-O.json
cmp /tmp/power-three-carry-certificates.json /tmp/power-three-carry-certificates-O.json
```

Explicit exceptions keep every mathematical and receipt check active under
`python3 -O`. The receipt also binds this checker's own source SHA-256.
